findings.title: Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly, so nothing is actually loaded lazily
findings.body: The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, … directly as property values. `import()` is invoked at module-evaluation time, so the moment anything imports `@calcom/app-store` all 28 app modules are requested and evaluated — exactly as before, only now asynchronously. The server/serverless bundle still contains every app and cold start still pays for loading all of them, so the PR's stated goal (async/lazy import of app packages) is not achieved while every call site has been forced to become `async`. To get real laziness the values need to be thunks (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) resolved on demand, ideally with memoization.

findings.title: Rejected app-module imports become unhandled rejections at module load
findings.body: All 28 `import()` promises are created when the module is evaluated, but most are never awaited (only the one app matching a credential/dirName is). If any app module throws while being evaluated (missing env var, bad top-level code, transitive import error), its promise rejects with no handler attached. In Node >= 15 an unhandled rejection terminates the process by default, so a single broken app module can take down the whole web/API server, and the failure is reported at module-init time with no connection to the call site that would have needed that app. Previously a failing app module produced a synchronous error on import of `@calcom/app-store`, which was at least attributable and contained.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials creates floating promises and changes the type of `calendar`
findings.body: `getCalendar(credential)` is now async, but it is still invoked unconditionally inside the `flatMap` before the `app.variant === "calendar"` check. For every non-`calendar` variant credential the returned promise is created and immediately discarded; if it rejects (e.g. the app module fails to load) it becomes an unhandled rejection, which can crash the Node process. In addition, the `calendar` property of the returned items is now `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`; this is a silent contract change for any consumer of `getCalendarCredentials()` other than `getConnectedCalendars` (which was updated), and such a consumer would call methods on a Promise at runtime. Move the `getCalendar` call behind the variant check and audit/convert all consumers.

findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are fire-and-forget and never awaited
findings.body: In the recurring/`allRemainingBookings` branch the credentials are iterated with `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); … apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })`. The callback's promise is discarded, so the `await getCalendar(...)` and the subsequent `calendar.deleteEvent(...)` calls run after `forEach` returns. By the time `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) copies `apiDeletes`, the array is still empty, so the handler returns "Booking successfully cancelled" without waiting for any external calendar event to be removed — in a serverless runtime the function can be frozen/torn down first, leaving cancelled recurring bookings still present on users' calendars. Errors from these calls also escape as unhandled rejections. The sibling non-recurring branch in this same diff was correctly converted to `for (const credential of …)`; this branch needs the same treatment (and should push the promise, not the awaited result).

findings.title: requestReschedule: calendar/video cancellation is now an un-awaited async forEach
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) … })` discards every callback promise. The mutation continues to send the reschedule-request email and webhooks and returns while the `getCalendar` import and the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls are still pending, so in a serverless environment the previous calendar entries and video meetings may never be deleted. Any error thrown inside the callback is now an unhandled rejection (it can terminate the process) rather than something the caller can observe. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))` instead.

findings.title: try/catch around the cancellation loop is dead code after converting the callback to async
findings.body: The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` was made `async` so it can `await getCalendar(...)`, but the callback's promise is thrown away. The enclosing `try { … } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }` can therefore never observe a failure from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`: those rejections surface as unhandled promise rejections (process-level crash risk in modern Node) and are silently lost from the logs. The function also returns `true` and sends the reschedule email before the deletions have completed, so the stale calendar/video entries may never be removed. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))` inside the try block.

findings.title: try/catch around the cancellation loop is dead code after converting the callback to async
findings.body: Same defect as in `vital/lib/reschedule.ts`: `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); … })` discards the callback promises, so the surrounding `try/catch` that logs errors can never fire, failures from `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` become unhandled rejections, and the function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return `true` before the external calendar/video entries have actually been deleted. Await the work explicitly (e.g. `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))`) inside the try block.

findings.title: Commented template entry points at a non-existent path
findings.body: The commented-out example was changed from `./_example` to `// example: import("./example")`. The app template directory is `_example`, so a developer copying this line as a guide for registering a new app will reference a path that does not exist. Keep the directory name accurate (`import("./_example")`).
